result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A rewords the result messages more clearly, gives a specific email error that says how to fix it, and relabels the button to "Signing you up…" while sending, which also gives the hidden spinner a text equivalent. B only disables the button, gives the spinner no text equivalent, and keeps the vague "Something went wrong" for server errors. B also makes Name required, which goes beyond the requested final touches. Both put the error in the shared status line rather than right next to the field, and both only slow the spinner for reduced motion instead of stopping it. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers add a status region, try/catch/finally, double-submit protection, aria-invalid with focus, darker colours and a slower spinner for reduced motion. B is better: its error and failure messages say how to fix the problem and that the typed values are kept, and the button changes to 'Signing you up…' as a text equivalent for the waiting state. A makes the name field required without being asked, leaves the spinner with no text equivalent, and its failure message is still generic.
